issues.legal_issue: A criminal complaint may be quashed under inherent jurisdiction when the surrounding circumstances show that it was maliciously instituted for an ulterior purpose arising from a private and personal grudge.
material_facts: The accused and complainant were relatives and neighbours, and a property dispute between the complainant and a member of the accused’s family was already pending.
Police attended a quarrel between the parties and initiated peace-maintenance proceedings against both sides on the day of the alleged incident.
The complainant first sought an investigation on the same allegations more than six weeks after the incident; that application was rejected for lack of sufficient grounds to register a case.

The complainant later filed a complaint repeating those allegations. An inquiry report found the allegations unproved, which the Court considered as part of the sequence of events and not as substantive evidence.
The complaint described two incidents on the same day, but the summoning court did not accept the allegation concerning the second incident.
issues.conclusion: The complaint proceedings were maliciously instituted with an ulterior motive arising from a private and personal grudge, and allowing them to continue would abuse the process of the court. The proceedings were quashed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the High Court may quash proceedings to prevent abuse of process or secure the ends of justice. Bhajan Lal identifies as a category warranting quashing a criminal proceeding manifestly attended by mala fides or maliciously instituted with an ulterior motive to wreak vengeance because of a private and personal grudge. State of Karnataka v. L. Muniswamy and State of Karnataka v. M. Devendrappa affirm the power to prevent abuse and advance justice; Sunder Babu v. State of T.N. and Vineet Kumar v. State of Uttar Pradesh apply the Bhajan Lal category. The power is to be exercised cautiously and is not a means to short-circuit a prosecution merely because an accused disputes the allegations.

rule.if: quashing_petition_in_criminal_proceeding and preexisting_private_dispute and bilateral_peace_proceedings and delayed_complaint and prior_similar_request_rejected and one_alleged_incident_not_accepted

predicates.quashing_petition_in_criminal_proceeding: An accused seeks to quash a criminal proceeding by invoking the court’s inherent jurisdiction.
predicates.preexisting_private_dispute: A private dispute between the complainant and the accused or a member of the accused’s family existed before the alleged incident.
predicates.bilateral_peace_proceedings: Authorities responded to a dispute on the day of the alleged incident by taking peace-maintenance action against both sides.
predicates.delayed_complaint: The complainant waited a substantial period after the alleged incident before first seeking formal criminal action on the allegations.
predicates.prior_similar_request_rejected: An earlier request seeking formal action on substantially the same allegations was rejected for lack of sufficient grounds.
predicates.one_alleged_incident_not_accepted: The court considering whether to summon the accused did not accept one of multiple incidents alleged in the complaint.

issues.definition: When an accused seeks to quash a criminal proceeding and the listed circumstances together indicate a private dispute, a delayed and previously rejected complaint, and doubt about part of the alleged occurrence, the proceeding is quashed.

issues.legal_issue: Rejection of a request for police investigation does not prevent the complainant from later pursuing a complaint before a court.
material_facts: An earlier application seeking police investigation on the alleged incident was rejected for lack of sufficient grounds to register a case.
A later complaint repeating the allegations was filed before the court, which summoned the accused.
issues.conclusion: The rejection of the earlier application seeking police investigation did not preclude the complainant from filing a complaint before the court.
issues.legal_principle: The Court stated that rejection of an application under Section 156(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure does not preclude a complainant from filing a complaint under Section 200 of the Code. The earlier revision had also left the complainant an alternative remedy of filing an appropriate application before the concerned court.

predicates.court_complaint_proceeding: A complainant pursues a complaint before a court rather than relying only on a request for police investigation.
predicates.prior_police_investigation_request_rejec: The complainant’s earlier request for police investigation into the same allegations was rejected.

issues.definition: When a complainant pursues a court complaint after an earlier request for police investigation was rejected, that rejection does not bar the court complaint.
